Agar theek na karwaya jaye tu nuqsaan: Engine oil kam hone ki wajah se turbocharger aur valve train ko proper lubrication nahi milti, jiss se engine seize hone ka ya engine bay mein aag lagne ka khatra paida ho sakta hai. ai_diagnosis_result.plain_english_explanation: The vehicle is experiencing an engine oil leak originating from the cylinder head area on the Honda Civic 1.5 Turbo. This is typically caused by a degraded or hardened cylinder head gasket or valve cover gasket due to extreme turbo operating temperatures and high boost pressure. If left unaddressed, it can lead to critical engine oil starvation, damage to the turbocharger system, smoking from the engine bay, and a severe fire hazard if oil drips onto the hot exhaust components. Al Shaheen Auto Hub will perform a complete teardown of the affected area, replace the failed seals with genuine OEM components, clean the mating surfaces, and pressure test the engine.
ai_diagnosis_result.mechanical_root_cause: Thermal degradation of the elastomeric cylinder head cover gasket and valve stem seals leading to loss of clamp load, resulting in external engine oil leakage around the cylinder head mating surface and spark plug wells on the L15B7 1.5L Turbo engine.

Torque all bolts to factory specifications using a calibrated torque wrench. / Factory torque specs ke mutabiq bolts tight karein. 7. Top up engine oil, clean any oil residue from the engine bay, and perform a comprehensive road test and pressure check. / Engine oil top up karein aur test drive lein.

ai_diagnosis_result.roman_urdu_explanation: Assalam-o-Alaikum Sir, Al Shaheen Auto Hub main aap ka khair khmaqdam hai. Aap ki Honda City (2.0 Turbo) main jo AC ka masla araha hai us ki mukamal tafseel darj zail hai: 1. AC Cooling ka Bilkul Na Hona: Masla aur Wajah: Customer ne bataya ke AC bilkul cooling nahi kar raha aur 0 cooling hai. Is ki buniyadi wajah ya toh AC compressor ki clutch engagement na hona, refrigerant gas ka mukamal leak hojana, ya phir AC system ke fuse/relay aur climate control module main koi electrical fault hona hai. Naye model ki turbo cars main electronic compressor aur pressure sensors hotay hain jin main wiring ya sensor ki kharabi ki waja se compressor on nahi hota. Agar theek na karwaya jaye tu nuqsaan: Garmi ke is mosam main bina AC ke gari chalana na sirf mushkil hai, balkay compressor bina lubrication aur load ke chale ya refrigerant na honay ki waja se mazeed kharab ho sakta hai jis se aap ka kharcha mazeed barh sakta hai. Al Shaheen ka Solution: Humari specialized AC service team sab se pehle computer diagnostic scanner ke zariye AC control unit ke fault codes check kare gi. Is ke baad Nitrogen pressure test ke zariye leak check kiya jaye ga aur agar gas leak hui toh usko seal kar ke, vacuum pump se system saaf kar ke R134a ya R1233zd refrigerant gas aur compressor oil dobara top-up kiya jaye ga.
ai_diagnosis_result.plain_english_explanation: The customer has reported a total lack of cooling from the AC system in their Honda City. Upon preliminary assessment at Al Shaheen Auto Hub, this points toward a complete loss of refrigerant pressure, a faulty AC compressor control valve, a blown relay/fuse, or a leak in the high/low-pressure aluminum lines or condenser core. Since the vehicle has low mileage, it may be a factory assembly defect, a stone hit puncturing the condenser, or an electrical communication failure. Our team will perform a complete pressure test, electronic scan, and leak detection to restore optimum climate control performance.
ai_diagnosis_result.mechanical_root_cause: Refrigerant pressure drop to zero due to potential condenser puncture from road debris, faulty electronic compressor control solenoid valve, loose harness connector at the pressure switch, or O-ring failure at piping joints.
ai_diagnosis_result.work_to_be_done: 1. Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner to check HVAC module for stored trouble codes (DTCs) related to AC pressure sensor or compressor lock. 2. Perform visual and ultraviolet (UV) dye inspection on AC lines, compressor seals, evaporator joints, and condenser core for potential leakage points. 3. Conduct a Nitrogen pressure test up to 150 PSI to locate micro-leaks in the plumbing or radiator/condenser assembly. 4. Evacuate the system using a professional vacuum recovery machine for at least 20 minutes to remove moisture and air contaminants. 5. Recharge the system with exact OEM specified quantity of R134a refrigerant and PAG oil. 6. Start engine, switch on AC to maximum, and verify high/low-side pressure gauges and cabin vent temperature.
